transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um… I guess I’m here because some nights I eat way more than I mean to. Like after grading papers, I’ll start with leftovers and then just keep going—cereal, crackers, peanut butter, even snacks I packed for my classroom. It… kind of scares me.
Do you feel like you can stop eating once you've started on those nights?
No… not really. Once I start, it’s like part of me is standing back saying, Joan, stop, this is enough, but I just… keep opening things and eating anyway, until I feel painfully full.
Do you feel guilty after these eating episodes?
I… I don’t really know how to answer that. I don’t feel good about it, I guess. It’s hard to talk about.
Do you feel like you're in control of what you're eating on those nights?
No… not really. Once I start, it’s like the sensible part of me is watching it happen and saying, Joan, stop. But I just keep… opening things, eating, until I’m really uncomfortably full.
Do you ever try to get rid of the extra calories after one of these eating episodes?

Sometimes… not like, um, throwing up or anything. But I’ll tell myself I can’t have breakfast or lunch the next day, and then I’ll stay out on the trail for hours… or do extra yoga, even if I feel shaky and completely worn out.
Have you ever made yourself throw up after one of these eating episodes?
No… I don’t make myself throw up. I’ve thought about… ways to undo it, I guess, but not that.
How often do these nights of eating more than you mean to happen?

It’s… pretty often. For the past few months, I don’t think there’s really been a week where it didn’t happen at least once. Usually one night, sometimes more, and then the next day I try to make up for it by not eating at school or pushing myself to walk a long time or do extra yoga.
How often do you do extra exercise or restrict your food intake to try to make up for the extra calories after one of these eating episodes?
Usually the next day. I… I’ll skip eating at school, or I’ll make myself do a really long walk or extra yoga. It’s been happening most weeks for the last few months, I guess.
Have you ever made yourself throw up after eating normally, not just after one of these episodes of eating more than you meant to?
No… I don’t think so. I haven’t made myself throw up after normal meals.
How many days a week do you typically restrict your food intake or do extra exercise to make up for the extra calories?

Maybe… three or four days a week? It depends. After one of those nights, I usually tell myself I can’t have breakfast or lunch at school, and then I’ll do a long walk or extra yoga later… even if I feel shaky or really tired.
How many times a week do you have one of these episodes where you eat more than you mean to?
Usually at least once a week… sometimes more. I don’t think there’s been many weeks lately where it didn’t happen at all.
Have you ever made yourself throw up after eating?
I’m not really sure how to answer that… I mean, I don’t think I have, no.
Have you ever made yourself throw up after eating?
I… I don’t think so. Not on purpose, no.
How often do you do something to try to make up for the extra calories after one of these eating episodes?

Most times, I guess. Like… if it happens at night, the next day I’ll usually skip eating while I’m at school, or I’ll make myself go on a long walk or do extra yoga. Lately there hasn’t been many weeks where that didn’t happen at least once.
Have you ever made yourself throw up after eating?
No… I don’t think I’ve done that. I mean, not made myself throw up.
Have you ever made yourself throw up after eating?
No… I haven’t done that. Not that I can remember.
Have you ever made yourself throw up after one of these eating episodes, even if it was just once?
I… no, I don’t think so. Not that I can remember, even once.
Have you ever made yourself throw up after eating?
I really don’t think so… I haven’t made myself throw up.
Do you do something to try to make up for the extra calories after every episode of eating more than you mean to?

Yeah… I guess I do. Not throwing up, but after one of those nights I’ll usually tell myself I can’t have breakfast or lunch at school. And then I’ll go walk or run on the trail for hours, or do extra yoga, even if I feel shaky and worn out.
Have you ever made yourself throw up after eating?
No… I haven’t done that. I know I already said, but… no, not throwing up.
